summary:
The First Wheels on the Moon (Apollo 15 - LRV): In 1971, humanity used a vehicle on the lunar surface for the very first time. Transported by the "Falcon," the Lunar Roving Vehicle (LRV) allowed astronauts to travel 27.9 km around the rugged Apennine mountains and collect over 77 kg of samples, unlocking ancient lunar secrets.

The First Robot on the Red Planet (Mars Pathfinder & Sojourner): In 1997, Mars Pathfinder landed in the Ares Vallis region of Mars by bouncing like a giant beach ball thanks to massive airbag systems. The tiny Sojourner rover that emerged analyzed Martian rocks, proving that Mars once had a warm, wet, and water-rich past.
Shared Legacy: Ranging from Apollo to Mars, these two pioneering missions laid the technological foundation that allowed humanity to travel miles across space and unlock the mysteries of the universe.
